correctness.rationale: For real distributional BV, signed-jump representation reduces the exact norm to one-jump errors. The uniform-marginal identity and beta-binomial tail formula yield \(E_n'(s)=2p_{n,j}(s)[j+1-(n+2)s]\). The binomial positive-part identity yields \(E_n(s_j)=2\binom nj s_j^{j+1}(1-s_j)^{n-j+1}\). Strict decay of ratios of \(a_k=(k+1)^{k+1}/k!\) proves central parity maxima. Opposite signs of distinct jump-error profiles on positive-measure intervals prohibit mixed extremizers. Stirling gives the limiting constant. Exact rational finite checks and approximate signed multijump tests passed; they are not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: No matching exact sharp finite Bernstein-Kantorovich \(BV\)-to-\(L^1\) error and parity-located extremizer theorem was identified in actual full-text and bibliographic searches. Kivinukk--Metsmagi 2011 proves convergence estimates in the variation seminorm for smoother inputs; Berdysheva et al. 2022/2024 derives broad L1 rates with nonsharp constants. Finta 2014 supplies modulus-of-smoothness Lp bounds. Related exact Bernstein and Durrmeyer norms treat different kernels and different norming jumps. This is a best-knowledge conclusion subject to inaccessible older results.

value.rationale: The classical cell-average Kantorovich polynomial is a natural positive reconstruction operator for integral sample data. The exact attained \(BV\)-to-\(L^1\) error constant provides a sharp finite-resolution calibration on discontinuities. The previously unquantified within-cell strict maxima and odd-degree two-point displacement are structural sampling effects; combined with a complete equality classification and Gaussian-scale limit they are more than a routine rate estimate or arbitrary numerical slice.
